stem:
Veer traces two angles on tracing paper. The diagram shows angle $P$ and angle $Q$ sharing vertex $O$.

Which claim correctly decides which angle is larger?

options.text: Angle $P$ and angle $Q$ are equal, because both rays start at $O$.
Angle $Q$ is larger than angle $P$, because overlaying with matching vertices shows $Q$ sticks out past $P$.
Angle $P$ is larger than angle $Q$, because overlaying with matching vertices shows $P$ sticks out past $Q$.
The sizes cannot be compared, because the angles use different letter names.

teacher.key_rationale: Overlay matching vertices: the wider opening is P, so P is larger than Q. Sharing O alone does not make them equal. Reversing the overlay result, or refusing comparison because of letter names, misses the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Two rays from O forming nested angles P (wider) and Q (narrower).
